Formed in 1864, it is the [[Oldest football clubs|oldest club in Wales]] and the [[Oldest football clubs|third-oldest professional football team in the world]].{{cite web|last1=Jones|first1=Peter|title=Wrexham AFC History|url=http://www.wrexhamafc.co.uk/club/history/|access-date=13 July 2025|archive-date=15 December 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121215212034/http://www.wrexhamafc.co.uk/club/history/|url-status=dead}}{{ cite news |title=The oldest professional Football Club in Wales |url=https://www.wrexhamafc.co.uk/club/history/ |publisher= Wrexham A.F.C. |url-status= dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220615022901/https://www.wrexhamafc.co.uk/club/history/ |archive-date=15 June 2022 |access-date= 9 August 2025 }}{{cite web |title=History and Honours |url=https://www.wrexhamafc.co.uk/the-club/history-and-honours |website=wrexhamafc.co.uk |publisher=Wrexham AFC |access-date=13 July 2025}} The club competes in the {{English football updater|Wrexham}}, the second tier of the [[English football league system]]. Domestically, the club has won the [[Welsh Cup]] a record twenty-three times, the short-lived [[FAW Premier Cup]] a record five times, the [[EFL Trophy|Football League Trophy]] in [[2005 Football League Trophy final|2005]] and the [[FA Trophy]] in [[2013 FA Trophy Final|2013]]. Recently, following five unsuccessful play-off campaigns in the [[National League (division)|National League]], Wrexham achieved three promotions in three seasons, from 2022 to 2025, through winning the [[2022–23 National League]], finishing runner-up in the [[2023–24 EFL League Two]] and also in the [[2024–25 EFL League One]]. Thus, Wrexham secured a spot in the [[2025–26 EFL Championship|EFL Championship]], and became the first club across the top five tiers of English football to achieve three consecutive promotions. Internationally, Wrexham competed in the [[UEFA Cup Winners' Cup|European Cup Winners' Cup / UEFA Cup Winners' Cup]] on multiple occasions through success in the Welsh Cup – reaching the quarter-finals once in [[1975–76 European Cup Winners' Cup|1976]], as well as beating [[FC Porto]] and drawing with teams such as [[Real Zaragoza]] and [[RSC Anderlecht|Anderlecht]] during their time in the competition. However, following changes made to the Welsh Cup competition in 1995, Welsh clubs playing in the English Football system (such as Wrexham) were no longer permitted to enter and therefore, had to qualify for European competition exclusively via the English system. In 2012, UEFA reiterated that Welsh clubs playing in the [[English football league system]] could not qualify for European competitions via the Welsh Cup, after Wrexham (alongside [[Merthyr Town F.C.|Merthyr Town]] and [[Newport County A.F.C.|Newport County]]) rejoined for one season in [[2011–12 Welsh Cup|2011–12]].{{Cite news |date=2012-06-20 |title=Welsh Cup snub for Wrexham and Newport County |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/18520092 |access-date=2025-07-15 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}{{Cite news |date=2012-03-21 |title=Uefa give Swansea and Cardiff European assurance |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/17459332 |access-date=2025-07-15 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}} Wrexham received major financial investment after its 2020 takeover by American actor [[Rob McElhenney]] and Canadian and American actor [[Ryan Reynolds]] through Wrexham Holdings LLC,{{Cite news |last=Weatherspoon |first=Chris |date=2025-05-07 |title=The BookKeeper – Exploring Wrexham's finances and how Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney run a club like no other |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6319873/2025/05/07/the-bookkeeper-wrexham-reynolds-mcelhenney-finances/ |access-date=2025-07-15 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}} starting a new era of success. This acquisition, alongside the global publicity of the ''[[Welcome to Wrexham]]'' documentary series, had a significant impact on the club's visibility, resulting in an unprecedented new international fanbase for a team that were in the fifth division (at the time).{{cite web |last=Scudder |first=Jake |date=26 September 2022 |title=Wrexham AFC: The fastest growing club in the world |url=https://www.soccerscene.com.au/wrexham-afc-the-fastest-growing-club-in-the-world/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221120215111/https://www.soccerscene.com.au/wrexham-afc-the-fastest-growing-club-in-the-world/ |archive-date=20 November 2022 |access-date=23 April 2023 |website=Soccer Scene.com}} The club's home stadium, the [[Racecourse Ground]], is the world's oldest international stadium that still continues to host international games.{{cite web |last1=Bagnall |first1=Steve |date=17 June 2008 |title=Guinness cheers Racecourse with official record |url=http://www.dailypost.co.uk/news/north-wales-news/guinness-cheers-racecourse-official-record-2830321 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150705093829/http://www.dailypost.co.uk/news/north-wales-news/guinness-cheers-racecourse-official-record-2830321 |archive-date=5 July 2015 |access-date=18 June 2008 |website=Daily Post Wales}} The record attendance at the ground was set in 1957 when the club hosted a match against [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] in front of 34,445 spectators.{{cite web |title=Wrexham v Manchester United, 26 January 1957 |url=http://www.11v11.com/matches/wrexham-v-manchester-united-26-january-1957-210986/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141129044907/http://www.11v11.com/matches/wrexham-v-manchester-united-26-january-1957-210986/ |archive-date=29 November 2014 |access-date=10 April 2014 |website=11v11.com}} The club's main rivalries are with English clubs [[Chester F.C.|Chester]], [[Shrewsbury Town]], and [[Tranmere Rovers F.C.|Tranmere Rovers]], with matches against Chester being known as the [[cross-border derby]].{{Cite web |last=Lewis |first=Thomas |date=2022-01-05 |title=We asked Wrexham fans who the club's main rivals were – here's what you said |url=https://www.dailypost.co.uk/sport/asked-wrexham-afc-fans-who-22643375 |access-date=2023-11-28 |website=North Wales Live |language=en}} In addition, Wrexham have been referred to as cup "giant-killers", due to unexpected successes against top-flight opponents, such as [[Wrexham A.F.C. 2–1 Arsenal F.C.|upsetting the reigning league champions]] [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] in the 1992 FA Cup."}}
